core_obligations: Write an arbitrary sheaf as a filtered colimit of subsheaves generated by finitely many sections over quasi-compact opens, and use the colimit formula for cohomology to reduce to the finitely generated case (proof lines 3548-3571).

Induct on the number of generators: split off one generator, apply the long exact sequence of a short exact sequence, and reduce to sheaves generated by at most one section, which are precisely the quotients of the extensions by zero of Z along quasi-compact opens (proof lines 3574-3587).

For such a quotient with kernel K, reduce again to K finitely generated by a filtered colimit argument, then use the filtration of the subsheaf K of the constant sheaf by extensions of extensions by zero to transfer the hypothesis to the successive quotients, and conclude for K and hence for the quotient by induction along the long exact sequence (proof lines 3589-3615).
proof_roadmap: Reduction to finitely generated sheaves (proof lines 3548-3571).
Induction reducing to one generator (proof lines 3574-3587).
The kernel, its filtration and the transfer of the hypothesis (proof lines 3589-3615).
difficulty_reason: Under four hypotheses on a topological space X, namely quasi-compactness, quasi-compact opens forming a basis, stability of intersections of quasi-compact opens, and the vanishing of the cohomology of the extensions by zero of the constant sheaf Z along quasi-compact opens above the degree d, the lemma concludes that the cohomology of every abelian sheaf vanishes above d (statement lines 3530-3545). The proof has three genuinely different stages. First the author writes an arbitrary sheaf as a filtered colimit of subsheaves generated by finitely many local sections over quasi-compact opens and uses the colimit formula for cohomology, reducing to the finitely generated case (proof lines 3548-3571). Second, an induction on the number of generators via a short exact sequence reduces to sheaves generated by at most one section, which are exactly the quotients of the extensions by zero of Z along quasi-compact opens (proof lines 3574-3587). Third, the kernel of such a quotient is controlled by the filtration of a subsheaf of the constant sheaf Z by extensions of extensions by zero, which transfers the hypothesis to the successive quotients and finishes by induction along the long exact sequence (proof lines 3589-3615). The claim is H3: three linked reduction stages, each of which is an argument of its own, ending in a transfer of the vanishing hypothesis along a filtration.
